look_here_first: Start with the leaves. Forestiera pubescens has noticeably broader elliptic to ovate leaves with some pubescence, and it is winter-deciduous. The rigid paired side branches still make the classic 'elbow' architecture.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora; Travis — UT Plant Resources Center herbarium specimens; Williamson — detailed county treatment of F. pubescens var. pubescens.

best_field_traits: subopposite to opposite branch pattern with rigid paired lateral branches
leaves elliptic to broadly lanceolate/ovate or obovate, much broader than F. angustifolia
leaf surfaces often with scattered short hairs
flowers appear before leaves and lack a corolla
morphology_keys.comparison_training: F. angustifolia has very narrow linear leathery leaves, often clustered on twigs, and is evergreen to semi-evergreen/drought-deciduous rather than winter-deciduous.

comparisons.key_distinctions: F. angustifolia has very narrow linear leathery leaves, often clustered on twigs, and is evergreen to semi-evergreen/drought-deciduous rather than winter-deciduous.
